newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 18.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Friday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Manila shares are likely to fall further mirroring losses in Wall Street and unlikely to get much support from the slight overnight gain of PLDT's ADR, Sun Hung Kai Securities Phils vice-president Raul Ruiz said.
* BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap said any strong recovery in the market is not likely in the short term due to continued foreign selling and lacklustre corporate developments.
* On Thursday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index ended lower by 33.10 points to 2,927.87.
* On Thursday, the Dow Jones dipped 21.27 points to 6,658.60. PLDT's ADR rose $0 1/8 to $58 1/2.

* The Philippine trade deficit widened to $1.96 billion in the first two months of the year compared with $1.582 billion in the same period last year which analysts in a Reuters poll said was within expectations.
* The Philippines' Board of Investments said investment proposals it approved for the first quarter of the year rose by 118 percent to 78.9 billion pesos.

* The Asian Development Bank (ADB) said it expects the Philippines' gross national product (GNP) to grow seven percent in 1997 and 1998 but said further fiscal consolidation and a cautious monetary policy are needed.
* International Container Terminal Services Inc said it expects net income this year to jump 22 percent from 1996 level of 474.74 million pesos.
* The Philippine National Bank said it expects trying times ahead despite its reported 467 million pesos net income in the first quarter against 340 million last year.
* PNB said net proceeds from the 60 percent sale of its subsidiary PNB-Republic Bank to Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) at a price of 880 million pesos would go to the building of its reserves.

* Oil refiner Petron Corp remains the market leader for the first three months of the year but its market share dipped to 41.9 percent from 42.6 percent the first quarter, the latest total oil inland trade data showed.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld said that Moody's Investor Service in a report said that Philippine banks may end up paying the same price of excessive growth and leverage that some other Asian banking systems are paying after their "bubble economies" burst.
* The peso closed lower at 26.355 to the dollar vs 26.353.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.03125 percent.
